learning_outcomes.text: Be able to solve problems related to fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Be able to use computer programs in the field of hydraulic installations and machines.
Be able to prepare technical reports to explain theoretical-experimental works on fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Be able to analyze, select, and predict the behavior of hydraulic machines and installations.
Be able to select hydraulic machines and plan hydraulic installations appropriately.
Be able to predict a transient with graphical methods and know its control systems.
Know how to calculate the main flow parameters in pipes and channels.
Know the current regulations related to fluid machines and installations.
Know the typical morphology of hydraulic networks, the different design criteria, and their modeling.
Know the problems of cavitation and be able to predict and avoid them.
Know the real behaviors of hydraulic machines, characteristic behavior curves, and applicable similarity laws.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to networks and their simulation
Examples of application of Bergeron's method
Theoretical head provided by a pump
Alternative derivation of the fundamental equation of turbomachines
Deviation from theoretical behavior. Definition of losses
Introduction to the application of similarity law to turbomachines
Net Positive Suction Head available (NPSHd) and Net Positive Suction Head required (NPSHr)
Operation of a pump with cavitation
Optimal inlet diameter in a centrifugal impeller to avoid cavitation
Similarity laws applied to the study of cavitation
Operating point of a pump in an installation
Introduction to the use of EPANET for simulation: branched networks (computer lab)
Simulation and analysis of mesh networks (computer lab)
Simulation and analysis of hydraulic transients and their protection (computer lab)
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum of 5 out of 10 points must be obtained in the overall qualification. The overall qualification is obtained by calculating the weighted average of the different parts: continuous assessment (40%) and final exam (60%). The final exam must be passed with a minimum of 5.0 points, or 4.5 points to compensate with continuous assessment, but the maximum grade if this is not met is 4.5. Practical work activities are recoverable in the second call by resubmitting work, while practical reports are not recoverable.
